name: Serpinopathy with Loss of Serpin Function

criteria.description: Demonstration of reduced functional serpin protein levels in plasma or tissues
Identification of pathogenic mutation in serpin gene associated with loss of function
Presence of characteristic clinical manifestations such as emphysema or liver dysfunction
Histological evidence of serpin polymer accumulation or deficiency in affected tissues

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic serpin gene mutation plus reduced serpin function and compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by family history and exclusion of other causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Early onset panacinar emphysema predominantly in lower lung lobes
searchTerms: lung damage causing emphysema from alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
early onset emphysema related to enzyme deficiency
chronic lung disease due to protein deficiency

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hepatic cirrhosis due to serpin polymer accumulation
pathognomonic.notes: Progressive liver fibrosis and cirrhosis in absence of other causes
searchTerms: liver scarring from abnormal protein buildup
chronic liver damage from protein deposits

common.notes: Chronic cough, dyspnea, and sputum production
searchTerms: breathing difficulty with chronic lung obstruction
symptoms of chronic bronchitis and emphysema

common.notes: Mild to moderate elevation indicating liver injury
Inflammation of subcutaneous fat presenting as tender nodules

occasional.notes: Yellowing of skin and sclera due to liver dysfunction
Localized swelling due to vascular leakage

occasional.symptomName: Chronic fatigue related to systemic inflammation
occasional.notes: Persistent tiredness not explained by other causes
searchTerms: chronic fatigue due to systemic inflammation

rare.notes: Elevated pressure in portal venous system secondary to cirrhosis
Increased pulmonary arterial pressure due to chronic lung disease
Occasional kidney dysfunction related to systemic effects

imaging: Chest CT showing panacinar emphysema predominantly in lower lobes
Liver ultrasound or elastography indicating fibrosis or cirrhosis
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in SERPINA1 or other serpin genes causing loss of function
other: Histopathology demonstrating serpin polymer accumulation in hepatocytes
Pulmonary function tests showing obstructive pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Similar genetic defect but may have variable serpin function loss
Liver disease without associated pulmonary emphysema

redFlags: Rapidly progressive respiratory failure in young adult
Early onset liver cirrhosis without other risk factors
references: Orphanet: Serpinopathy with loss of serpin function - ORPHA:250811
